classification.difficultyReason: Directly translate each stated count into success, X and n, obtaining p by elementary outcome counting or a single complement.

content.prompt: For each binomial context, define success, define $X$ in words, state $n$ and $p$, and write $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)$.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
A fair die is rolled 45 times.
The number of times it shows a number greater than 4 is recorded.

answer.short: Success: showing 5 or 6. $X$ is the number of rolls showing more than 4. $n=45$, $p=\frac13$; $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(45,\frac13)$.
answer.worked:
Success is showing 5 or 6. Let $X$ be the number of the 45 rolls showing more than 4.
$$\begin{aligned}n&=45\\p&=\frac26=\frac13\\X&\sim\operatorname{Bin}(45,\tfrac13)\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Seven per cent of a large batch of seeds fail to germinate. Forty seeds are planted.
The number that germinate is recorded.

answer.short: Success: germinating. $X$ is the number of the 40 seeds that germinate. $n=40$, $p=0.93$; $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(40,0.93)$.
answer.worked:
Success is a seed germinating. Let $X$ be the number of the 40 seeds that germinate.
$$\begin{aligned}n&=40\\p&=1-0.07=0.93\\X&\sim\operatorname{Bin}(40,0.93)\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt:
A student guesses all 25 questions of a true/false quiz.
The number answered incorrectly is recorded.

answer.short: Success: answering incorrectly. $X$ is the number of the 25 questions answered incorrectly. $n=25$, $p=0.5$; $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(25,0.5)$.
answer.worked:
Success is an incorrect answer. Let $X$ be the number of the 25 questions answered incorrectly. Random guessing gives one incorrect option out of two.
$$\begin{aligned}n&=25\\p&=\frac12=0.5\\X&\sim\operatorname{Bin}(25,0.5)\end{aligned}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt:
A card is drawn from a shuffled deck, recorded, and replaced. This is repeated 18 times.
The number of picture cards (J, Q, K) drawn is recorded.

answer.short: Success: drawing a picture card. $X$ is the number of picture cards in 18 draws. $n=18$, $p=\frac{12}{52}=\frac3{13}$; $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(18,\frac3{13})$.
answer.worked:
Success is drawing a picture card. Let $X$ be the number of picture cards in 18 draws. A standard deck has 3 picture cards in each of 4 suits; replacement keeps the probability constant.
$$\begin{aligned}n&=18\\p&=\frac{3\times4}{52}=\frac3{13}\\X&\sim\operatorname{Bin}(18,\tfrac3{13})\end{aligned}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt:
In a large city, 62% of adults hold a driver’s licence. Fifty adults are chosen at random.
The number without a licence is recorded.

answer.short: Success: not holding a licence. $X$ is the number of the 50 adults without a licence. $n=50$, $p=0.38$; $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(50,0.38)$.
answer.worked:
Success is an adult not holding a licence. Let $X$ be the number of the 50 adults without a licence.
$$\begin{aligned}n&=50\\p&=1-0.62=0.38\\X&\sim\operatorname{Bin}(50,0.38)\end{aligned}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt:
A basketballer with a free-throw rate of 0.85 takes 16 shots, resting fully between each.
The number she misses is recorded.

answer.short: Success: missing a shot. $X$ is the number of the 16 shots missed. $n=16$, $p=0.15$; $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(16,0.15)$.
answer.worked:
Success is a missed shot. Let $X$ be the number of the 16 shots missed.
$$\begin{aligned}n&=16\\p&=1-0.85=0.15\\X&\sim\operatorname{Bin}(16,0.15)\end{aligned}$$
